The Complete Deep Cleaning Checklist for DFW Homes

A deep clean gets to the places a weekly tidy never touches. Here's our room-by-room checklist for DFW homes, plus a few tips for tackling it yourself.

Get My Instant QuoteCall (469) 210-8005

Published 2026-10-20 · Salt of the Earth Cleaning Co.

A regular clean keeps a home looking good. A deep clean resets it. It's the visit where you stop working around the dust on top of the ceiling fan and the line of grime along the baseboards and actually take care of them.

Homes around Dallas–Fort Worth have a few extra reasons to need one. Spring brings a coat of pollen on every sill. Summer means the AC runs constantly and moves dust through every vent. Kids and pets track in dirt year-round. Then the holidays arrive and suddenly you're hosting. Here's the checklist we work from, room by room, so you can do it yourself or know what to expect when you book.

Before you start

A deep clean goes faster when you work top to bottom and dry to wet. Dust falls, so start high (ceiling fans, light fixtures, blinds) and finish with the floors. Do your dusting and vacuuming before you bring out the spray bottles and mop.

Gather your supplies first: microfiber cloths, a soft scrub brush, an old toothbrush for grout and tight corners, a vacuum with a crevice tool, a mop and the cleaners you trust. If you have pets or little ones, choose eco-friendly, pet-safe products.

What a deep clean includes

Our deep clean includes everything in our standard clean, plus the extra detail below. This is our actual checklist, room by room.

Every room

  • Dust ceiling fans and light fixtures
  • Dust blinds
  • Wipe down window sills
  • Wipe light switches and outlet covers
  • Spot-clean walls and baseboards
  • Empty trash cans and put in fresh liners
  • Vacuum floors and rugs
  • Mop hard floors

Window sills are worth the extra attention here in North Texas, where spring pollen settles on them fast.

Kitchen

The kitchen is where grease and crumbs build up in places you don't see every day.

Counters, cabinets and sink

  • Clean and disinfect countertops
  • Scrub the backsplash
  • Wipe cabinet fronts and handles; inside of cabinets wiped too if they're empty
  • Clean and disinfect the sink

Stove and appliances

  • Clean the stovetop and drip pans
  • Wipe the outside of the range hood
  • Wipe the outside of the fridge, oven and microwave
  • Wipe the inside of the microwave
  • Clean inside the oven
  • Clean inside the refrigerator

If you're doing it yourself, save the oven and fridge for last, since they take the longest.

Bathrooms

Bathrooms are where a deep clean really shows.

  • Scrub and disinfect the toilet: bowl, tank, base and seat
  • Scrub shower walls and floor, or the bathtub
  • Remove soap scum from the shower and tub
  • Scrub the grout in bathroom tile
  • Clean and disinfect the sink and countertop
  • Wipe the vanity and cabinet fronts
  • Clean mirrors
  • Wipe towel bars and the toilet paper holder
  • Fold the end of the toilet paper roll for a finished look
  • Mop the floor

Soap scum and hard water build-up come off more easily if you let the cleaner sit for a few minutes before you scrub.

Bedrooms

  • Dust all furniture surfaces, including headboards
  • Wipe nightstands and dressers
  • Wipe ceiling fan blades
  • Clean mirrors and glass surfaces
  • Make the bed or change the linens (if you leave fresh ones out)
  • Vacuum the floor, including under the bed and along the edges

Living and common areas

  • Dust shelves, tables and décor
  • Wipe the TV screen with a microfiber cloth
  • Wipe the TV stand and entertainment console
  • Vacuum upholstered furniture
  • Fluff and straighten couch cushions
  • Clean glass surfaces and picture frames
  • Vacuum floors and rugs and mop hard floors

How often does a home need a deep clean?

Many homes do well with a deep clean once or twice a year: once in spring after pollen season, and once before the holidays. It's also the smartest first step before you start a recurring schedule. Once the home is at a clean baseline, regular visits keep it there with much less work.

If you're moving, an empty home calls for an even more thorough clean. Our move-in / move-out cleaning builds on this list with extras like door frames, inside vanities and closet shelving.

DIY or professional?

You can absolutely tackle this checklist yourself. Plan on a full weekend for an average home, and break it up by room so it doesn't feel overwhelming.
